thesis: T1 Energy (formerly FREYR Battery) is a pure-play U.S. solar domestic manufacturer building America's first fully integrated silicon solar supply chain. G1_Dallas (~5 GW module capacity) is operational and drove FY2025 revenue to $755.3M (from $2.94M in FY2024), while the ~2.1 GW G2_Austin cell fab is under construction and targeted online by Q4 2026. The pending ~$32M acquisition of KORE Power pushes TE into battery energy storage (BESS) and data center infrastructure, diversifying beyond solar modules. Section 45X manufacturing credits underpin margins, but high leverage (~178% D/E), FY2025 net loss of -$380.8M, and short-seller scrutiny keep this a high-risk, high-reward speculative name.

drivers: G2_Austin comes online ~Q4 2026, completing a fully integrated U.S. silicon supply chain
KORE Power acquisition opens BESS and data center infrastructure markets, re-rating the multiple
Section 45X manufacturing credits monetized, supporting record gross margins and adjusted EBITDA
Comprehensive G2 financing closes on favorable terms, removing balance-sheet overhang
Domestic-content premium and tariff/FEOC dynamics favor U.S.-made modules over Chinese supply

base_case.assumptions: G1_Dallas sustains ~5 GW run rate; G2_Austin financing closes and production starts near Q4 2026 with some slippage; KORE Power deal closes and contributes modest 2027 revenue; 45X credits partially monetized; one further capital raise likely. Consensus average 12-month target ~$10.07.

risks: Balance-sheet stress forces further highly dilutive financing
Policy changes weaken or eliminate Section 45X benefits
G2_Austin construction or financing stalls, or KORE Power integration disappoints
Chinese oversupply crashes solar module prices and margins
Short-seller thesis (Fuzzy Panda) proves out; volatility (beta 2.17) drives a de-rating

catalysts.event: Q2 2026 earnings — margin trajectory, G2 financing update, KORE Power integration plan
KORE Power (~$32M) acquisition close — entry into BESS and data center infrastructure
Comprehensive G2_Austin financing close — removes near-term balance-sheet overhang
G2_Austin (~2.1 GW cell fab) production start — fully integrated U.S. supply chain

key_risks: High leverage (~178% D/E) and thin liquidity (current ratio ~1.25) despite the $125M convertible raise
FY2025 net loss of -$380.8M; path to sustained profitability unproven
Policy dependency on Section 45X credits and domestic-content requirements
Execution and integration risk on G2_Austin and the KORE Power acquisition
Elevated short-seller and volatility risk (Fuzzy Panda report May 2026; beta 2.17)
Intense competition from profitable, well-capitalized First Solar and low-cost Chinese suppliers
